props.heading: Any CLI works — Claude Code, Codex, whatever ships next year.
props.body: The workflow doesn't depend on a proprietary interface. You address a decision by its ID in the decisions.json, write your override, and the pipeline re-renders only the affected beat. The rest stays unchanged.

props.heading: Patch, never regenerate.
props.body: Override a palette and only the affected beats are re-rendered; the audio is preserved; the timing stays. This is the difference between surgical editing and starting over. A five-second color change should not require a twenty-minute full rebuild.

props.heading: Now predict the hard case.
props.body: You override an accessibility default — specifically, you want a color combination that fails WCAG contrast for aesthetic reasons. What does the pipeline do? Commit to an answer before the reveal.

props.heading: It dissents, then complies — and logs it.
props.body: Contrast drops to 3.8:1 for this beat, logged in decisions.json with the override noted. The system tells you what you've decided and what the consequence is. It doesn't block you; it informs you. You remain the judge.

props.body: The Medhavy MCP server treats creators as adults: inform, don't block.
